A \(T\)-tetromino covers \(4\) squares.

### 1. Upper bound
By area alone,
\[
N\le \left\lfloor\frac{36}{4}\right\rfloor=9.
\]

Color the \(6\times6\) board like a checkerboard. Each \(T\)-tetromino covers three squares of one color and one square of the other, so its black-minus-white imbalance is either \(+2\) or \(-2\).

If nine \(T\)'s fit, they cover all \(36\) squares. The board has \(18\) black and \(18\) white squares, so its imbalance must be \(0\). However, the sum of nine numbers, each equal to \(+2\) or \(-2\), cannot be \(0\). Thus nine \(T\)'s cannot fit, giving
\[
N\le 8.
\]

### 2. Construction with eight
The following arrangement uses eight \(T\)'s; equal letters form one \(T\), and dots are uncovered squares:
\[
\begin{array}{cccccc}
A&A&A&B&E&\cdot\\
D&A&B&B&E&E\\
D&D&C&B&E&H\\
D&C&C&C&H&H\\
F&F&F&\cdot&G&H\\
\cdot&F&\cdot&G&G&G
\end{array}
\]

Hence eight can be placed, and nine cannot. Therefore the maximum is

\[
\boxed{8}
\]
